content.text: : replaces iron, found in hemoglobin, myoglobin, and other enzymes; allows the transportation of oxygen via hemoglobin
: MC product for oral replacement therapy
ADRs: constipation, darkens stool, nausea, epigastric pain
Black Box Warning: accidental OD of iron-containing products is a leading cause of fatal poisoning in children <6yo – keep product out of reach of children
: delivers iron as ferritin; dissociates upon uptake from the gastrointestinal tract allowing iron and maltol to be absorbed separately
: iron replacement product for the tx of iron deficiency in adults
: hemochromatosis & other iron overload syndromes; pts requiring repeated blood transfusions
: flatulence, diarrhea, constipation, discolored feces, abdominal pain/discomfort/distention
: avoid use if IBD flare is present, danger of iron-overload in children
: released ferric ion is transported by transferrin and incorporated into Hb or storage sites
: dyspnea, hypotension, neurological sxs, N/V, flushing, pruritis
: anaphylactic-type reactions, including fatalities, have followed the parenteral use of iron dextran – test dose required
: treatment of iron deficiency anemia in chronic hemodialysis patients (>6yr) receiving supplemental erythropoietin therapy
: treatment of iron-deficiency anemia in CKD, including nondialysis-dependent patients (with/without receiving erythropoietin therapy) and dialysis-dependent patients receiving erythropoietin therapy
: treatment of iron-deficiency anemia in adults with CKD
: treatment for adult patients who either cannot tolerate or have not responded well to oral iron; iron deficiency anemia (IDA) in adult patients with non-dialysis-dependent CKD
: B12 deficiency in several conditions, including maintenance therapy following IM therapy and HIV, AIDS, and Crohn’s disease
: maintenance therapy of pernicious anemia after normalization of B12 levels with injectable B12
: glycoprotein manufactured through recombinant DNA technology and has the same actions as erythropoietin

: chemotherapy-induced anemia, anemia associated w/ CKD, anemia due to zidovudine, pediatric anemia in children undergoing dialysis for CKD, reduction of allogenic blood transfusion in surgery (elective, noncardiac, nonvascular) patients at high risk for perioperative transfusion with significant, anticipated blood loss
: CKD (high BP, HA, arthralgias, nausea), HIV (fever, fatigue, HA, cough, diarrhea, rash, nausea, skin reactions, congestion, dizziness), allergic reactions
: anemia associated w/ CKD both on & off dialysis, anemia in pts w/ non-myeloid malignancies where anemia is due to the effect of concomitantly administered chemotherapy

: patients treated with ESA and dosed to a target hemoglobin concentration of 13.5 g/dL were at a significantly increased risk for serious and life-threatening CV complications (death, MI, hospitalization for CHF, stroke) compared to patients dosed to a target Hb of 11.3 g/dL – FDA recommends a target Hb in the range 10-12 g/dL and not to exceed 12 g/dL; patients have an increased risk of serious CV events and death when these products are dosed to target Hb > 12 g/dL

: in cancer patients with certain tumor types (ie, breast, non-small cell lung, head and neck, lymphoid, cervical), ESAs shortened overall survival and/or increased the risk of tumor progression or recurrence in some clinical studies – in patients with cancer, use the lowest ESA dose needed to avoid RBC transfusions and serious cardiovascular and thromboembolic reactions

: use ESAs only for treatment of anemia due to concomitant myelosuppressive chemotherapy, and discontinue following the completion of a chemotherapy course – patients receiving myelosuppressive chemotherapy should not be treated with ESAs when the anticipated outcome is cure
: antineoplastic agent/antimetabolite: ribonucleotide reductase inhibitor that prevents DNA synthesis and has been used in chemotherapy regimens
: for use by adults with recurrent moderate or severe painful crises (≥3 in the preceding 12mo) to reduce the frequency of crises and the need for blood transfusions
: myelosuppression, leukemia, opportunistic infections, teratogenic (high doses)
